Refresh a single-layer point GeoPackage's coordinate columns

Source: R/bag_gpkg_refresh.R
bag_gpkg_refresh.Rd

Reads a one-layer point GeoPackage, optionally refreshes its UTM columns with bag_assign_utm(), optionally applies a caller-supplied transformation, optionally writes the result back over the GeoPackage, and writes .csv and .RData backups.

Usage

bag_gpkg_refresh(
  path_gpkg = NULL,
  dir_backup = "data/backup/",
  update_utm = TRUE,
  fn_site_id = NULL,
  write_back_to_path = FALSE,
  write_to_csv = TRUE,
  write_to_rdata = TRUE,
  return_object = FALSE,
  ...
)

Arguments

path_gpkg

character Path to a GeoPackage holding exactly one point layer. More than one spatial layer is refused, since which to refresh would be decided by layer order. Support tables carrying no geometry — QGIS's layer_styles, for one — are not counted, and survive the write-back.

dir_backup

character Directory for the backups. Created if absent.

update_utm

logical Refresh the UTM columns with bag_assign_utm(). Default TRUE.

fn_site_id

A function applied to the data after the UTM step, or NULL (default) to apply nothing. It is called as fn_site_id(dat) and must return the data.

This is where the fish-passage package's site-id assignment is injected. That logic is about site identity rather than about files, so it stays in that package and is passed in rather than imported — neither package depends on the other.

write_back_to_path

logical Overwrite the layer in path_gpkg with the result, keeping its name. Default FALSE. Only that layer is replaced, so a style saved into the GeoPackage is left alone.

write_to_csv

logical Write a geometry-dropped .csv backup. Default TRUE.

write_to_rdata

logical Write an .RData backup holding the object under the GeoPackage's base name. Default TRUE.

return_object

logical Return the updated object. Default FALSE.

...

Passed to bag_assign_utm().

Value

The updated sf object when return_object is TRUE, otherwise NULL invisibly. Called for the files it writes.

Details

It is named for the refresh rather than for the backups because write_back_to_path = TRUE overwrites path_gpkg. The backups are a side effect, not the contract.

Both backups exist on purpose. The .csv is the versionable one; the .RData holds the object exactly, because rebuilding it from the csv introduces small differences.

See also

bag_backup() for a plain file copy, and bag_assign_utm() for the coordinate step.

Other files: bag_backup(), bag_gpkg_to_geojson(), bag_layers()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# refresh the coordinate columns and hand the object back, writing nothing
updated <- bag_gpkg_refresh(
  path_gpkg = file.path(tempdir(), "form_fiss_site_2026.gpkg"),
  write_to_csv = FALSE,
  write_to_rdata = FALSE,
  return_object = TRUE,
  # passed through to bag_assign_utm()
  col_easting = "utm_easting",
  col_northing = "utm_northing",
  sig_dig = 3
)
} # }
